decisions.reason: Because the accelerator program builds on the firm's existing advisory and partnership capabilities and the firm has strong in-house R&D to absorb and use outside knowledge, management would likely keep it despite it being somewhat less central than core machinery products.

Management would likely keep the bio-based binder because it still builds on the firm's recycling and feedstock knowledge and its R&D base supports learning, but its material-product character is somewhat farther from the firm's core equipment business and raises commercial uncertainty.

The infectious waste decontamination plant is close to the firm's established modular treatment technology, remains prominently marketed, and fits a growing R&D-intensive business where management can interpret results and improve the product.
